VITA.01.note: NHGRI explains epigenomic marks, gene regulation, development, environmental response, and the limited senses in which marks can persist through cell division or generations.

exercise.prompt: Draw how DNA methylation and histone modification can alter gene expression without changing nucleotide sequence, then distinguish mitotic from transgenerational inheritance.

VITA.02.note: NHGRI's genome-editing overview explains targeted cutting and repair, why CRISPR changed the field, and the difference between research use and clinical application.

exercise.prompt: Sketch a CRISPR-Cas9 edit from guide-RNA targeting through DNA cutting and repair, comparing knockout by end joining with precise editing by a repair template.

VITA.03.note: This review balances established roles in metabolism and immunity with unresolved definitions of a healthy microbiome and uncertainty about whether many associations are causes or consequences.

article.title: Establishing What Constitutes a Healthy Human Gut Microbiome: State of the Science, Regulatory Considerations, and Future Directions
article.source: National Academies workshop authors — PubMed Central

exercise.prompt: Take one microbiome-health headline and classify its evidence as association, mechanism, animal experiment, or human causal trial, noting plausible confounders.

VITA.04.note: OpenStax presents the evidence that mitochondria and plastids descend from engulfed bacteria, including membranes, DNA, ribosomes, and gene transfer.

exercise.prompt: Create an evidence table for endosymbiosis covering double membranes, circular DNA, ribosomes, binary fission, phylogeny, and transferred nuclear genes.

VITA.05.note: DeepMind's official AlphaFold overview explains sequence-to-structure prediction and its scientific impact while leaving experimental validation and protein dynamics visible as separate problems.

exercise.prompt: Look up one protein in AlphaFold DB and identify high- and low-confidence regions, then list questions a static prediction cannot answer about function or dynamics.

VITA.06.note: CDC explains antigens, adaptive immune memory, vaccine platforms, and why temporary immune symptoms differ from the disease being prevented.

article.title: Explaining How Vaccines Work
article.source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

exercise.prompt: Trace antigen presentation, helper T-cell signalling, B-cell activation, antibodies, and memory cells after vaccination, then compare first and later exposure.

VITA.07.note: OpenStax distinguishes convergent from divergent evolution and shows how similar selection pressures can independently produce analogous traits.

exercise.prompt: Compare wings in bats, birds, and insects, distinguishing shared function, developmental origin, homology, analogy, and the selection pressure involved.

VITA.08.note: OpenStax connects chloroplast structure, pigments, light reactions, carbon fixation, and energy storage in a standard biology treatment.

exercise.prompt: Draw the light reactions and Calvin cycle, labelling where photons, water, oxygen, ATP, NADPH, carbon dioxide, and carbohydrate enter or leave.

VITA.09.note: WHO's current fact sheet explains natural selection for resistance, misuse and overuse, transmission across humans, animals and environments, and the public-health consequences.

exercise.prompt: Model a bacterial population before and after antibiotic exposure and explain selection, mutation, horizontal transfer, incomplete treatment, and transmission without saying bacteria choose to adapt.

VITA.10.note: NIGMS explains molecular clocks, the suprachiasmatic nucleus, peripheral clocks, environmental cues, and the consequences of chronic misalignment.

article.title: Circadian Rhythms
article.source: National Institute of General Medical Sciences

exercise.prompt: Track light exposure, meals, exercise, sleepiness, and sleep timing for three days, then identify cues that may advance, delay, or desynchronise your clocks.

VITA.11.note: NIA explains telomeres as chromosome-end protection and places shortening among several interacting ageing processes rather than presenting it as a single master clock.

exercise.prompt: Draw the trade-off between unlimited cell division and tumour suppression, including telomere shortening, telomerase, senescence, apoptosis, stem cells, and cancer.

VITA.12.note: OpenStax gives a quantitative account of resting potential, threshold, voltage-gated sodium and potassium channels, refractory periods, and propagation.

exercise.prompt: Plot membrane voltage over time and label rest, threshold, depolarisation, repolarisation, hyperpolarisation, sodium-channel state, potassium-channel state, and refractory periods.
